rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the overall elution window, detect any unretained or strongly retained compounds, and avoid truncation while giving usable selectivity information across the full mixture.

All 10 peaks eluted well within the gradient, so trim the gradient window to the actual elution region to reduce time penalty while keeping all peaks inside the gradient. This should test whether a narrower, better-focused window preserves the already excellent resolution and improves CRF.

The broad window was clearly better, and all peaks are already well resolved, so the main opportunity is reducing run time. A steeper version of the successful scout will test how much resolution margin we can trade for faster elution and a higher CRF.

The critical cluster around peaks 5–7 lost too much resolution at 10 min, while 20 min had ample margin but unnecessary time cost. An intermediate gradient should recover enough separation for that slope-sensitive cluster while likely retaining a zero time penalty.

The limiting pair improves strongly with shallower slope, and 14 min is already near-optimal with no time penalty. A small increase to 16 min should test whether the critical pair can be pushed to baseline resolution while still keeping CRF at or near the maximum.

Since 15 min is unavailable on the grid and 14 vs 16 min bracket the slope optimum, the next lever is temperature. Lowering T slightly from the current best method may improve selectivity for the stubborn 6/7 pair without increasing run time much.

Temperature clearly changes selectivity enough to move the critical overlap, so try the opposite direction from 35 C while keeping the best slope. This tests whether slightly higher T resolves the cluster better than 40 C without adding time penalty.

The best result is at 14 min, but the time term is already zero, so the objective is to increase the resolution term toward 1.000. A 12 min run will map the slope-response more finely around the optimum and confirm whether 14 min is truly the best grid point or whether the CRF peak is broader than it appears.

The critical pair improves monotonically with shallower slope, and 16 min already achieved full resolution with only a tiny time penalty. Testing 18 min will show whether the resolution term remains at 1.000 while the added time cost is still small enough to surpass the current best CRF.

The full 0.05–0.95 window is likely broader than needed, and the last peak elutes well before the gradient ends. Narrowing only the high-organic end slightly while keeping the successful slope/time combination may improve selectivity in the critical mid-cluster without pushing the late peak into an excessively long hold.

Reducing phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved CRF, suggesting the gradient window was indeed too broad. A further small reduction in phi1 may continue to sharpen selectivity in the critical 6/7 region while keeping all compounds within the gradient and time penalty at zero.

The best region is now centered near phi1 = 0.90, and the only remaining limitation is the 6/7 pair. Combining that improved window with a slightly steeper 12 min gradient will test whether the window change, rather than longer tG, is what drives the higher CRF and whether a faster method can still retain near-optimal selectivity.

The first peak is not close to unretained, so slightly raising phi0 may better center the gradient on the occupied elution window while preserving the successful phi1 and tG. This tests whether trimming unused low-organic range improves selectivity in the crowded middle cluster enough to beat the current best.

Raising phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved CRF further, indicating the low-organic start was still broader than needed. A small additional increase to 0.15 may better focus the populated elution window and nudge the critical 6/7 pair higher while likely keeping the run comfortably short.

The best region appears near phi0 = 0.10 and phi1 between 0.85 and 0.90. Testing the combined trim at both ends may slightly improve selectivity in the crowded center while preserving the essentially optimal run time.

A CRF of 1.000 is the maximum, so we should preserve the current best while using remaining injections only to map robustness nearby. Stepping phi1 down one more notch from the optimum tests how sharply the maximum is localized on the high-organic boundary.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so further runs should only probe nearby robustness around the optimum. This combination keeps the successful phi1 while offsetting the slightly broader window at lower phi0 with a shallower slope, checking whether an alternative local optimum also reaches the ceiling.

The maximum CRF is already achieved, so use the remaining budget to test local robustness against a small temperature change around the optimum while keeping the fully resolved window. A lower temperature with a slightly shallower gradient may reveal an alternative plateau of top-performing methods.

The optimum is clearly centered at 40 C, but with the maximum already secured, a single symmetric temperature check around the best phi-window is still useful to confirm robustness. This tests whether the local maximum is sharp in T or if there is any equally good high-temperature plateau.

The top method is secured, so use the remaining budget to map the nearby response surface systematically. This checks whether the lower-temperature selectivity shift that hurt at 16 min behaves differently under a steeper slope, clarifying whether the 5/6 vs 6/7 tradeoff is primarily thermal or slope-dependent.

With the optimum already found, this completes the local temperature/slope map around it. Comparing 12 min at 35, 40, and 45 C will isolate whether temperature mainly shifts the identity of the critical pair or also changes slope sensitivity near the best phi-window.

The optimum at 0.10/0.85/14/40 is already established, so this final local check tests whether the maximum is broad toward slightly higher phi0 when phi1 is held at the best value. It refines robustness at the low-organic boundary without moving away from the known best temperature and slope.

We now know the optimum extends at least to phi0 = 0.15 with the best phi1, tG, and T. One more step higher in phi0 tests the upper edge of that plateau and whether the low-organic start can be trimmed further without sacrificing the maximum CRF.

Two methods already achieve the maximum, so use one of the last injections to test whether the optimum plateau also extends to a slightly lower phi1 when paired with the improved phi0 = 0.15. This maps the high-organic edge of the best-performing region more cleanly than revisiting temperature or slope.

For the final injection, probe the last untested corner near the proven optimum plateau by pairing the higher phi0 with the higher phi1. This cleanly defines whether the maximum-CRF region extends diagonally across the trimmed phi-window space.
